question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${r}^{2}$ and $100$ are both perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{{r}^{2}}{100}} & =\sqrt{\frac{{r}^{2}}{{10}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{r\cdot r}{10\cdot 10}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{r}{10}\cdot \frac{r}{10}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{r}{10})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{(\frac{r}{10})}^{2}} & =|\frac{r}{10}| \\  & =\frac{|r|}{|10|} \\  & =\frac{|r|}{10}\end{aligned}
$$
